latest_findings.claim: In the one completed seed (74; 4L d128, e<=0.5, m2 in [0.1,1], 5000 steps), force does beat a best-of-5 control at the end: layer-4 R2 = 0.689 vs control 0.480, a margin of 0.210 against a required 0.1 (spread 0.041). But it does not form late. Its trajectory margin is already 0.124 at the first checkpoint (step 500) and stays above the bar at every later checkpoint (formed_at_step 500). It keeps rising (0.124 → 0.210, +0.086) while accel_step levels off (layer-4 R2 0.960 vs control 0.780; margin 0.160 → 0.180, +0.020). Force leads on raw margin (0.21 vs 0.18), but accel_step leads clearly once each margin is divided by its headroom (0.82 vs 0.40).
latest_findings.confidence_note: Only one seed counts. Seed 73 (run-20261012-102821-56c8) failed when the worker restarted at about step 4000, so it has no probes, and the hypothesis needed both seeds. The seed-74 results are mixed. Three of the expected-if-true conditions hold: the final force margin is at least 0.1 against best-of-5 controls, accel_step is above its bar at step 500, and force gains 0.086 between steps 500 and 5000, just over the 0.08 threshold. The fourth fails: force formation at step >= 1000. Neither expected-if-false condition is met, so the earlier ~0.22 single-control force margins were not artifacts in this setup. With checkpoints every 500 steps, we cannot tell whether force forms at about step 100 alongside accel_step or somewhere in 100-500. What would change the verdict: (1) a second seed with the same config showing a final force margin >= 0.1 and a gain >= 0.08 would support 'force keeps strengthening late' as a replicated result, while still refuting 'forms late'; (2) finer early checkpoints (every 50 steps to 1000) showing force first persistently above the bar after step 300 would revive the late-formation claim; (3) the force margin collapsing once distance and accel_step are regressed out of the target would mean the late gain is a sharpening of those codes, not physical force.

latest_findings.claim: At e in [0, 0.8] (N=64, 4L, d64, 600 steps), the headroom-normalised layer-4 accel_step margin, (R2 - control)/(1 - control), at step 600 is 0.475 for seed 70 (R2 0.670 vs best-of-5 control 0.372), 0.455 for seed 71 (0.671 vs 0.396) and 0.475 for seed 72 (0.672 vs 0.375). All three seeds fall inside the predicted [0.44, 0.53] band, and their controls and raw R2 values fall inside the predicted ranges. That puts e<=0.8 between the cited e<=0.7 value (~0.55-0.58) and the e<=0.85 value (~0.38-0.41). Force is much weaker by the same measure: raw margin 0.124-0.150 at layers 1-2 (R2 0.31-0.42 vs control 0.19-0.27), normalised 0.15-0.21, persistent formation late at steps 250-400 and still rising at step 600. accel_step formed at steps 50-100 and levels off at a raw margin of 0.275-0.298.
latest_findings.confidence_note: All 3 seeds completed (none stopped) and land in the predicted band with little spread (0.455-0.475), and the controls are tight (spread 0.011-0.022, so required_margin is 0.1). Four things limit the claim that the decline is gradual. (1) The e<=0.7 and e<=0.85 reference values come from other experiments, and the e<=0.85 value rests on only 2 seeds. (2) With only three ceiling values (0.7, 0.8, 0.85), 'gradual' cannot be told apart from a decline that steepens: the normalised drop is ~0.09 over 0.7->0.8 but ~0.07 over 0.8->0.85, and raw R2 falls ~0.13 over 0.7->0.8 but ~0.11 over 0.8->0.85, which per unit of e looks like steepening. (3) The [0.44, 0.53] band is wide enough to hold several curve shapes. (4) Every arm shares data_seed 0. An e<=0.75 arm far from the interpolated value would change the picture. So would a different data_seed moving the e<=0.8 normalised margin out of the band, for example to >=0.54 or <=0.43. Either could show a step rather than a smooth decline.

latest_findings.claim: At N=16 (L=4, d=64, 3000 steps, e<=0.5), the accel_step margin does not rise above the N=64 reference; it sits at the low end of that range. accel_step R2 is 0.941 vs control 0.810 (margin 0.131, layer 2) in seed 20 and 0.936 vs 0.795 (margin 0.140) in seed 21. Headroom-normalized margins are 0.69 and 0.68, below the predicted 0.8 and level with the ~0.70 at N=64. Force leads accel_step on raw margin: 0.733 vs 0.497 (margin 0.236) in seed 20 and 0.767 vs 0.492 (margin 0.275) in seed 21. Both seeds beat the baseline by a wide margin (val_mse_ratio 0.0007).
latest_findings.confidence_note: The accel_step part of the prediction is refuted in both seeds. Raw margins of 0.13-0.14 miss the >=0.25 target and fall inside the expected-if-false band. Normalized margins of 0.68-0.69 are below the 0.75 cutoff. The force part is mixed. Seed 21's force margin of 0.275 is 0.015 above the expected-if-false band (0.12-0.26). Seed 20's 0.236 is inside it. Only seed 21 meets the force >=0.25 target. So the verdict rests on accel_step, the quantity the hypothesis said next-step prediction needs. Force may still increase with coarser sampling: the sibling N=256 arm gives force margins of only 0.03-0.04, while its normalized accel_step margin is about 0.66-0.73, also flat. Two caveats limit the comparison. First, the N=64 reference runs (run-20261011-202614-*) used single controls and may differ in training length. A matched N=64 arm with the same seeds, 3000 steps and best-of-3 controls would be needed to call accel_step flat across N. Second, accel_step's control R2 at N=16 (0.80-0.81) is the highest we have seen, which caps the raw margin. In the trajectories, accel_step crosses 0.1 at step 500 (0.112 and 0.117), the first checkpoint where val_mse_ratio < 1, but formed_at_step reports 1000. That is the known one-checkpoint lag. The verdict would change if a matched-control N=64 arm showed normalized accel_step margins well below 0.68.

latest_findings.claim: At N=256 (4 layers, d_model=64, 3000 steps, e <= 0.5, m2 in [0.1, 1]), the two gravity probes split. accel_step beats control by more than at N=64: margin 0.231 (R2 0.880 vs control 0.650, layer 4) and 0.245 (0.911 vs 0.666, layer 3). force does not beat control: margin 0.040 (0.526 vs 0.486) and 0.033 (0.541 vs 0.508). Distance margin is 0.67-0.69 and val_mse_ratio is 0.24-0.32. The paired N=16 arm runs the opposite way on both probes: accel_step margin 0.13-0.14, force margin 0.24-0.28.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The hypothesis predicted that accel_step and force would move together, and they did not. accel_step clears the expected-if-false bar (>= 0.15) in both seeds. That refutes the claim that fine sampling removes the per-snapshot acceleration code. force falls below the expected-if-true bar (<= 0.12) in both seeds. Both seeds show the same split, so the pattern is reproducible, but neither prediction holds as stated. Much of the accel_step margin trend across N comes from the controls. accel_step control R2 falls from about 0.80 at N=16 to 0.65-0.67 at N=256, and raw R2 actually drops slightly (0.94 to 0.88-0.91). The headroom-normalized margin, (R2 - control)/(1 - control), is flat: about 0.69 at N=16 and 0.66-0.73 at N=256. The force decline is not a control effect. Force controls are about 0.49-0.51 in both arms, while raw force R2 falls from 0.74-0.77 to 0.53-0.54. So at fine sampling the model keeps a per-snapshot acceleration code but loses the m2-weighted physical-force signal. The N=64 reference values come from older single-control runs, so the comparison with N=64 is approximate. Formation timing cannot be resolved: every probe crosses at the first checkpoint, step 500. Unlike the 600-step N=256 runs, these beat the constant-velocity baseline, but only after step 1500. The verdict would change with a matched N=64 arm under the same best-of-3 controls and 3000 steps. If that arm's force margin were also about 0.04, the force loss would not be specific to N=256. If it were about 0.2, steps_per_orbit would be shown to remove the force signal.

latest_findings.claim: In the L=2, d_model=32, n_systems=1000 cell, both new seeds reproduce the seed-0 ordering. Seed 1: force R2 0.603 vs control 0.382 (margin 0.221, layer 1), accel_step R2 0.827 vs control 0.681 (margin 0.146, layer 2). Seed 2: force 0.643 vs 0.388 (margin 0.255), accel_step 0.780 vs 0.652 (margin 0.128). So force has the larger raw margin while accel_step keeps the higher raw R2, and val_mse_ratio is 0.064 and 0.079. Through training the force margin keeps rising (0.112 to 0.221 and 0.136 to 0.255 from step 500 to 3000), while the accel_step margin levels off at 0.13-0.15 by step 1500.
latest_findings.confidence_note: All four expected-if-true conditions hold in both seeds. Both runs completed 3000/3000 steps, and the force control_spread (0.049-0.064) is below the 0.1 bar, so required_margin is 0.1. Counting seed 0, three seeds now agree on the raw-margin ordering. The ordering depends on the metric, though. The accel_step control (0.65-0.68) is much higher than the force control (0.38-0.39), which leaves accel_step less headroom. On headroom-normalized margin, (R2 - control)/(1 - control), accel_step leads in seed 1 (0.46 vs 0.36) and force leads in seed 2 (0.42 vs 0.37). So 'force beats accel_step' holds only for raw margin. Force peaks at layer 1, the same layer where distance is decoded at R2 0.84-0.85. That means the force margin may be a nonlinear read of distance rather than an m2-weighted force; this run does not test that. All seeds share data_seed 0. Two things would change this verdict: a seed where the accel_step raw margin matches force, or a result showing the force margin disappears once distance is regressed out of the force target.

config.expected_if_false: In at least one seed, the final force margin is < 0.1 against best-of-5 controls (the earlier 0.22 margins were single-control artifacts), or the force margin at step 5000 is within 0.03 of its step-500 value in both seeds (no late formation).
config.expected_if_true: In both seeds, the final force margin over the best-of-5 control is >= max(0.1, control_spread) at some layer, and the force margin read from the per-checkpoint trajectory first stays at or above the bar persistently at step >= 1000. accel_step is already persistently above its bar at the first checkpoint (step 500). The force margin at step 5000 exceeds the step-500 force margin by >= 0.08 in both seeds.
config.hypothesis: Physical force forms late. In long-trained 4-layer d_model=128 models (5000 steps, e in [0, 0.5], m2 in [0.1, 1]), the force probe beats a best-of-5 random control at the end of training, and its persistent formation step comes well after accel_step's. Earlier single-control runs (f-20261011-201533-0653) showed the force margin growing from ~0.1 to ~0.22 over 4000 steps. Every best-of-5 run so far stopped at 300-600 steps and showed no lasting force margin (0.00-0.08).

experiment.expected_if_false: In at least one seed, the final force margin is < 0.1 against best-of-5 controls (the earlier 0.22 margins were single-control artifacts), or the force margin at step 5000 is within 0.03 of its step-500 value in both seeds (no late formation).

The force margin at step 5000 exceeds the step-500 force margin by >= 0.08 in both seeds.
